requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.references.rust_item_selectors` that needs implementation evidence. The requirement has no implementation edges and no review roots were supplied.

Each clause describes observable outline output:
- "identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file, such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`" fixes the selector strings produced. Another parser or walker that produced the same selectors would satisfy it.
- "MUST NOT resolve Rust modules across files" limits behavior. Any implementation that never follows `mod x;` into other files satisfies it.
- "Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions, traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern blocks MUST be outline nodes" says which items appear in the outline. The outline is the observable result, not a prescribed data structure.
- "Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`" and "`use` declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous" fix the naming format. They do not fix how the names are computed.
- "Selector spelling MUST be documented" is a documentation obligation, not a code structure.

The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type or delegation interface. The tree-sitter requirement belongs to the cited `requirements.references.outlines`, which is context here and not the subject. Tests supply evidence for the behavioral obligations.

behavioral: The supplied tests cover each observable obligation in `requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`, and their assertions enforce the expected outcomes. I did not request implementation source.

- **Selector segments from syntactic ancestry.**
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` asserts that every selector in the list is produced. It also asserts that each selector resolves back to a node carrying that selector.
  - The list includes `fn[outer]`, `struct[Thing]`, `mod[local]/fn[run]` and `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`.
  - `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` repeats the same checks on a smaller source.
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes]` asserts the exact selector list for nested items.
- **No cross-file module resolution.** `functions_in_a_separate_module_file_are_selected_within_that_file` checks two files:
  - `lib.rs` containing `mod local;` yields only `mod[local]`.
  - `local.rs` containing `pub fn run() {}` yields exactly `fn[run]`, with no `mod[local]` prefix.
- **Required outline node kinds.** `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` asserts selectors for each kind the requirement lists:
  - functions (`fn[outer]`) and methods (`impl[Thing]/fn[run]`);
  - structs, enums and unions (`struct[Thing]`, `enum[E]`, `union[U]`);
  - traits (`trait[Trait]`) and impls (`impl[Thing]`);
  - modules (`mod[local]`, `mod[external]`) and macros (`macro[make]`);
  - constants, statics and type aliases (`const[C]`, `static[S]`, `type[Alias]`);
  - extern blocks (`extern[C]/fn[puts]`, `extern[Rust]/fn[other]`).
- **Impl naming.** The tests assert these forms:
  - `impl[Thing]/fn[run]` (self type only);
  - `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]` (self type and trait);
  - `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` (generic self type);
  - `impl[Thing/core::fmt::Display]` (qualified trait path);
  - `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]/fn[edge]` (non-path self type, percent-encoded).
- **Anonymous items.**
  - `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` asserts that two `use` declarations get distinct `use@…` selectors.
  - `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` asserts `macro@<12 hex>` selectors for item-position macros, both at top level and inside an impl or mod. It also asserts they are distinct from each other. It asserts that expression macros inside function bodies are not nodes by checking the total node count of 7.
- **Documented selector spelling.** `every_profile_mapping_is_documented` checks that `md/reference.md` contains the Rust selector spellings (including `use@…` and `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`). It also checks that anonymous `use` and macro invocations and the no-cross-file-module rule are documented.

I found no obligation without a test and no assertion that contradicts the requirement. All of the tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. When validating outline evidence inputs, Habeas MUST report
the line of the first syntax error in a recovered outline. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline, except
that a Markdown profile MAY additionally recognize colon-fenced directive
containers under {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fence_precedence`
and expose them as outline nodes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fenced_blocks`. Such containers MUST
preserve source ranges and containment, and MUST NOT be recognized within
literal code or raw HTML. Other nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline
descendants appear under the nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
